rationale: The hypothesis posits that original reports (specifically citing Chelban et al., 2017) described intellectual disability as universal and moderate-to-severe, whereas later reports identified preserved intellect. In reality, the literature shows that Chelban et al. documented individuals with normal cognitive development and mild intellectual impairment from the outset, while concurrent and subsequent cohorts identified through intellectual disability screenings (such as Anazi et al., 2017 and Lan et al., 2025) and hypomyelinating leukodystrophy cohorts (Baldi et al., 2018) highlighted severe psychomotor delay and developmental regression. A comprehensive synthesis across 25 individuals (Chelban et al., 2018, 2019) demonstrated a continuous clinical spectrum ranging from severe neonatal global psychomotor delay to childhood-onset progressive spastic ataxia with largely preserved intellect.

evidence.text: NKX6-2-related disorder exhibits a broad clinical spectrum ranging from severe neonatal-onset global psychomotor delay and spastic tetraplegia to childhood-onset slowly progressive spastic ataxia with a predominantly motor presentation and relatively preserved cognition.

source.quote: Our data reveal a phenotype spectrum with neonatal onset, global psychomotor delay and worse prognosis at the severe end and a childhood onset with mainly motor phenotype at the milder end.

evidence.text: In the summarized cohort of 25 individuals with NKX6-2 variants, cognitive involvement varied considerably; affected patients exhibited mild intellectual disability, and at least one individual had completely normal cognitive function.

source.title: Expanding the clinical and genetic spectra of NKX6‐2‐related disorder
source.quote: Our patients share a primary diagnosis of psychomotor delay, and they show spastic quadriparesis, nystagmus and hypotonia. Seizures and dysmorphic features (observed in 2 families each) represent an addition to the phenotype, while developmental regression (observed in 3 families) appears to be a notable and previously underestimated clinical feature.

conflicts: Chelban et al. (2017/2018) did not define intellectual disability as universally moderate-to-severe; rather, they documented preserved normal cognition in some individuals and mild impairment in others.

Ascertainment bias accounts for much of the divergence in reported cognitive phenotypes: cohorts recruited via intellectual disability genetics (e.g., Anazi et al., 2017) emphasize profound cognitive deficiency, whereas cohorts ascertained via adult and pediatric spastic ataxia panels report preserved intellect with severe motor disability.

new_directions.question_text: Does residual transcriptional repressor activity of NKX6-2 homeodomain missense variants correlate with preserved cognitive function versus profound psychomotor delay?
new_directions.rationale: Comparative studies such as Baldi et al. (2018) noted an absence of clear genotype-phenotype correlation using standard variant classifications; standardized functional in vitro assays evaluating homeodomain DNA-binding affinity could establish whether preserved cognition stems from partial hypomorphic alleles.

new_directions.question_text: What specific MRI hypomyelination patterns or MR spectroscopy markers differentiate NKX6-2 leukodystrophy with preserved intellect from classic Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease and other hypomyelinating leukodystrophies?
new_directions.rationale: Because nystagmus, hypotonia progressing to spasticity, and cerebellar ataxia overlap heavily with Pelizaeus-Merzbacher disease (PLP1) and Pol III-related leukodystrophies, systematic volumetric and diffusion-tensor imaging across cohorts could identify pathognomonic neuroimaging signatures.
